methods.note: Paper describes reinforcement learning-based floorplanning with PPO [7] and RND [8] exploration bonus, but critical methodological details are missing: (1) Complete RL training procedure including episode structure, state space definition, action space constraints, network architectures (CNN feature encoding layer specifications), training hyperparameters (learning rate, batch size, clip range); (2) Fast thermal model derivation lacks mathematical rigor—claims 'linear and time-invariant (LTI) system' approximation of thermal resistance network but provides no transfer function, impulse response validation, or stability analysis; (3) Self-thermal resistance table generation procedure incompletely described—how is single HotSpot run per design configuration chosen? What power density map is used? (4) Mutual-thermal resistance 1D lookup characterization versus distance lacks physical justification and validation methodology; (5) Microbump assignment algorithm references [4] without reproducing methodology; (6) No ablation studies isolating contribution of fast thermal model, RND bonus, or reward function components

code.note: GitHub repository mentioned ('More details can be found at the github') but URL is incomplete and inaccessible from packet. Without code access: (1) Cannot verify RL network architecture (CNN layer dimensions, kernel sizes, stride, pooling specifications); (2) Cannot reproduce thermal model implementation or validate LTI system assumptions; (3) Cannot verify action masking mechanism for infeasible chiplet placements; (4) Cannot confirm reward function implementation matches mathematical formula R = −λ × W − µ × (max(T−T₀,0))^α / (1+e^(−(T−T₀))); (5) Cannot verify PPO and RND integration; (6) Cannot validate synthetic dataset generation procedures or train/validation splits

parameters.note: Extraction identifies critical hyperparameter values as missing from paper: (1) Reward weighting parameters λ and µ—stated as 'weights' in Section II.C but no values provided, yet TABLE I and III report specific reward scores requiring these values; (2) Temperature limitation T₀—used in reward function but value unspecified despite being essential for thermal constraint tuning; (3) Gradient smoothing parameter α—controls penalty scaling at T=T₀ but value absent; (4) RL training hyperparameters (learning rate, network architecture specifics, batch size, number of epochs mentioned as '600 epochs' in TABLE I footnote but no formal specification); (5) PPO hyperparameters (clip range, entropy coefficient, value function coefficient) not stated; (6) RND bonus coefficient unspecified; (7) Fast thermal model assumes 2D self-thermal resistance table from HotSpot—resolution (grid spacing), interpolation method not documented; (8) Mutual-thermal resistance 1D table spacing and interpolation scheme not defined. Paper states results achieved with unspecified parameter tuning, making reproducibility impossible

config.note: Benchmark configuration claims contradicted by missing essential details: (1) Multi-GPU System [4], CPU-DRAM System [5], Ascend 910 System [6]—all three benchmark definitions reference external papers [4], [5], [6] not included in packet; paper does not reproduce chiplet count, dimensions (x_m, y_m, width_m, height_m), or layout constraints; (2) Five synthetic systems mentioned in Section III.B but not detailed in packet—'synthetic systems' architecture, power distributions, and thermal boundary conditions undefined; (3) Interposer thermal properties (thickness, material, thermal conductivity, heat sink model) not specified despite being critical for 2.5D thermal analysis; (4) Ambient temperature and cooling solution specifications missing; (5) Microbump assignment algorithm configuration references [4] without local reproduction; (6) Action masking mechanism for infeasible placements not formally defined—what constitutes infeasibility? (7) Sequential placement order policy undefined—how are chiplet ordering priorities determined?

data.note: Essential data for reproduction unavailable: (1) Multi-GPU System benchmark—complete floorplan geometry (chiplet coordinates, dimensions) for reference [4] not provided; individual chiplet power values (watts per chiplet) unspecified; interconnect pin locations and connectivity graphs missing; (2) CPU-DRAM and Ascend 910 benchmarks—same omissions apply; (3) Five synthetic systems dataset not documented—generation parameters, power distributions, thermal boundary conditions absent; (4) Validation dataset of '2,000 synthetic chiplet systems' described in Section III.A but not provided; no train/test split documentation; (5) HotSpot thermal models (node graphs, boundary conditions) generated for self-thermal resistance tables not archived; (6) No dataset link or supplementary material repository accessible from packet; (7) TABLE II thermal model validation uses 'Ground Truth' from HotSpot but actual HotSpot configuration files, thermal models, or mesh parameters not supplied; (8) Reward function optimization trajectories and convergence data not presented; (9) Individual run results across epochs not shown—only final aggregated statistics in TABLES I and III provided

findings.reason: Paper claims fast thermal model simplifies thermal resistance network to 'linear and time-invariant (LTI) system' but provides no mathematical derivation, transfer function, stability proof, or validation against dynamic transient behavior. Self-thermal resistance table generation from single HotSpot run lacks justification for why single-point characterization suffices. Mutual-thermal resistance 1D table versus distance lacks physical basis.
findings.locator: Page 2, Section II.C, paragraph on 'physical-informed fast thermal model'

findings.reason: Section III.A states '2,000 synthetic chiplet systems' used for thermal model validation in TABLE II but dataset is not supplied. No train/test split documentation, generation methodology, or access link provided. Reported MAE of ±0.25 K cannot be independently verified without raw data.
findings.locator: Page 2, Section III.A; TABLE II caption mentioning '2,000 synthetic chiplet systems'

findings.reason: TABLE I footnote states TAP-2.5D with fast thermal model 'takes a similar amount of time as training RLPlanner for 600 epochs' but does not specify total wall-clock time for TAP-2.5D with fast thermal model separately. Runtime fairness comparison between methods unclear—RLPlanner runtime (e.g., 20910 s for Multi-GPU) represents 600-epoch training, but TAP-2.5D comparison point is conflated.

TABLE II reports fast thermal model MAE of 0.2523 K (rounded to ±0.25 K in paper text). However, TABLE I results for Multi-GPU System show RLPlanner temperature of 91.15 °C with claimed MAE ±0.25 K, implying ground-truth uncertainty band of [90.90, 91.40] °C overlaps with baseline TAP-2.5D(HotSpot) value of 91.68 °C. Statistical significance of 0.53 °C improvement (91.68 - 91.15) is within claimed error margin, undermining claimed superiority.
findings.locator: Page 2, TABLE I and TABLE II; text claiming '20.28% improvement'

findings.reason: Reward function formula uses dimensionless wirelength W (97742 mm) and temperature T (91.15 °C) with unspecified scaling weights λ and µ to produce reward score of -37.1263. Without λ and µ values, the relative contribution of wirelength versus temperature optimization is unclear. TABLE III shows reward variation across cases (Case1: -5.8288 to -10.0058) but scaling basis undefined.

findings.reason: Fast thermal model uses self-thermal and mutual-thermal resistance tables suggesting steady-state analysis, but paper does not explicitly confirm whether 2D steady-state temperature is appropriate or if 3D transient dynamics are needed for chiplet-based systems. Physical mismatches note indicates 'no transient thermal dynamics' but this is not explicitly validated against application requirements.

findings.reason: TABLE I shows TAP-2.5D with fast thermal model achieves reward -41.3358 (Multi-GPU), worse than TAP-2.5D with HotSpot (-42.4572), despite being same algorithm. This performance reversal suggests fast thermal model error (MAE ±0.25 K) introduces biased optimization; however, paper does not address why swapping thermal solvers degrades TAP-2.5D performance or whether same hyperparameters were used.
